evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; entries for 奶, 女, 乃
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 奶 as 女 semantic + 乃 phonetic, with the initial sense ‘breast’; it also gives examples for ‘milk’ and ‘nurse/breastfeed’ from chapters 34, 19, and 20 of 初刻拍案驚奇 and 紅樓夢. The page supplies no dates for these works, so the examples establish cited usage but not an earliest attestation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: Reports a Qing-period account that a bronze-inscription graph pronounced 乃 meant ‘milk’, and that 奶 may have arisen after that graph was misread as 乃 and 女 was added. This is a competing historical explanation, presented there via later sources rather than demonstrated by inspected bronze evidence; the dictionary itself says the graph references for 奶’s oracle-bone and bronze forms are unpublished.
evidence.title: [A00879] 奶 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 聽雨叢談, 卷11, section 乳母 (Qing text hosted by Wikisource)
evidence.text: The text says that Beijing usage called wet nurses 奶子/奶媽 and cow’s milk 牛奶, and argues that 奶 may derive from a bronze graph pronounced 乃 meaning ‘mother; milk’, subsequently confused with 乃 and given 女. This is a late antiquarian report and conjecture, not an inspected early inscription or dated first use.
evidence.title: 听雨丛谈/卷11

evidence.source: 說文解字 online transcription with 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The received 說文 entry gives 乃 as ‘曳詞之難也’ and explains its shape as breath emerging with difficulty; the page also records ancient and seal forms. This describes 乃 separately and does not itself establish its ancient pronunciation as the phonetic source in 奶.
evidence.title: 說文解字「乃」

evidence.source: Chinese Academy of Sciences, 漢字「奶」：基本資料
evidence.text: Lists senses milk, breast, nipple-like object, breastfeeding, and infant-stage; records Mandarin reading nai3. It is a modern dictionary record and does not provide chronology for these senses.
evidence.title: 漢字「奶」：基本資料

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese page (recording references to 大字源, 漢語大字典, 辭海 and Unihan)
evidence.field: 字形拆解; modern and historical readings
evidence.text: The page groups 奶 in the 乃 phonetic series, records modern Mandarin nǎi and Cantonese naai1/naai5, and notes Min Nan variants ling/ne/nai. Its table says 奶 has no Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction there; the dossier’s Zhengzhang value *rneːlʔ is not independently validated by this page. These are readings from different varieties/systems and are not by themselves proof of an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: 奶 - 維基詞典

evidence.text: The local dataset has two 乃 entries: nǎi / Middle Chinese nojX / Old Chinese *nˤə(ŋ)ʔ (‘your’) and nǎi / nojX / *nˤəʔ (‘then’). No 奶 row was found in the searched local file. The system notation is preserved exactly; these 乃 entries are insufficient to demonstrate the compound’s historical sound relation. No verified character-specific upstream page for these local rows was established.
evidence.title: 奶 - 維基詞典 (comparison page; not an upstream dataset record)

The local full Unihan_Readings.txt lookup produced no matching 奶 or 乃 rows; the HSK extract did not supply the missing record.

evidence.field: A00879; 說文釋形、釋義、形體資料表
evidence.text: Says 奶 is not recorded in 說文. It lists breast as a colloquial sense, milk, nursing extended to rearing, and infant-stage use; its literary examples include 《兒女英雄傳》, 《紅樓夢》, 《海上花列傳》 and 《初刻拍案驚奇》, without dating them on this page. The listed oracle-bone and bronze reference materials are marked unpublished.
evidence.title: [A00879] 奶 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: Analyzes 奶 as 女 semantic plus 乃 phonetic, with breast as the gloss. It cites 《初刻拍案驚奇》卷34 for breast, 《紅樓夢》第19回 for milk, and 第20回 for nursing. The page does not give dates for the works, so these examples attest cited usage but do not establish the first attestation or a chronology of sense development.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: Reports a Qing-era account, attributed to 《通俗編》 quoting 《直語類錄》 and 《直語補證》, that a bronze graph pronounced 乃 meant ‘乳’. The dictionary treats 𠂏 as a variant of 奶 in one reading and also notes its relation to 乳. This is a later report, not direct evidence inspected here for the alleged inscription, its date, or its reading.
evidence.title: [A00879] 奶 - 教育部《異體字字典》研訂瀏覽

evidence.field: Chinese; Glyph origin and modern reading
evidence.text: Reports Zhengzhang-style Old Chinese reconstructions *rneːlʔ for 奶 and *nɯːʔ for 乃, and gives a phonosemantic analysis 女 + 乃. These are secondary-source reconstruction assertions, not direct inscription evidence. The values differ in their segmental forms, so this page alone does not establish the historical sound relation; its competing reconstruction system should not be merged with local Baxter–Sagart data.
evidence.title: 奶 - Wiktionary

gaps: No directly inspected oracle-bone, bronze, seal, or manuscript specimen for 奶 was found. The official Taiwan dictionary lists several ancient-form resources for 奶 as unpublished, so graphic development and any proposed corruption/addition of 女 remain unresolved.

The reported bronze graph pronounced 乃 with the sense ‘milk’ is quoted through Qing-era and modern reference accounts; its glyph identity, date, and independent sound evidence were not established. Do not collapse this account into the standard phonosemantic analysis as settled fact.

The accessible sources do not establish earliest attested date for 奶 or date the quoted 初刻拍案驚奇 and 紅樓夢 examples in the entry itself. The Qing text reports common Beijing use but is not a first-use record.

The exact local Baxter–Sagart rows exist for 乃 but not 奶; system-matched comparison for both characters is therefore unavailable. The secondary table also lacks a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for 奶. The dossier’s Zhengzhang reconstruction is not validated here.
Official Unihan character-specific records for U+5976 and U+4E43 could not be opened. No attempt was made to turn the failed request into verified Unihan evidence.

No reliable chronology was established linking ‘breast’ to ‘milk’, ‘breastfeeding’, wet nurse, or infant-related uses. The sources attest/define multiple uses but do not document the historical semantic transitions.
No reuse/license review was performed for repeated source material; the CUHK character page was paraphrased and cited, with no local extract recommended.

No directly inspected oracle-bone, bronze, seal, manuscript, or early printed specimen for 奶 was found. The Ministry character dictionary marks its oracle and bronze form references unpublished; graphic development and the proposed misreading/addition of 女 remain unresolved.
The account of a bronze graph pronounced 乃 meaning milk is reported through later sources. The object's identity, date, original reading and connection to 奶 were not independently established.

The consulted pages give undated literary examples or source titles without establishing which is earliest. No chronology was established for breast, milk, nursing/wet nurse, infant-stage, or the relation among these senses.

The phonosemantic analysis 女 + 乃 is asserted by CUHK and other dictionaries. In this pass I did not verify period-matched readings from primary phonological sources for both characters; the dossier's local Baxter–Sagart checks are not an inspected external upstream record. Current Mandarin readings could not be verified against official Unihan records because both endpoints failed.

No suitable historical glyph image was identified. The Commons chart was inspected but excludes 奶, and the Xiaoxuetang homepage was not a character-specific glyph record. Therefore no image is proposed; this is a specific provenance/identity gap, not evidence that no usable image exists.
No bulk extract or source mirroring is recommended. The recurring dictionary pages were paraphrased; no explicit bulk reuse permission was verified for their text.
